<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-drago-838b0a34" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-58adcfc64a04a3e1">What kind of apparent success does DRAGO guard against when an LLM converts a natural-language problem to a formal specification?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adrago">Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The model can produce a parseable, solvable specification that omits requirements, and the solver will faithfully solve the wrong problem. DRAGO uses localized diagnostics to constrain repairs rather than taking any solution as proof the original problem was solved. Formalization and solving need separate checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A schedule must assign both people. Omitting one person makes the scheduling problem easier, but that apparent success exposes a formalization error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22568">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22568-drago/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-58adcfc64a04a3e1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:drago" data-paper-title="Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6e1c82bffcc2da5">Why doesn&#x27;t a satisfiable result prove that a formal specification faithfully captures the task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adrago">Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The solver checks only the constraints that were written. It cannot tell whether a natural-language requirement was omitted or substituted. DRAGO diagnoses vocabulary contracts, reachability probes, and alignment with the task separately. Repairs must strictly reduce blockers without gaming the check by dropping goals. A probe that runs out of budget must report unknown, not proven unsatisfiable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A task requires reaching two places, but a specification listing only one can still be satisfiable. Removing the harder goal makes solving easier without repairing the specification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22568">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22568-drago/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6e1c82bffcc2da5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:drago" data-paper-title="Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-43baaeea36e72a90">Why can&#x27;t delete relaxation and full BFS substitute for one another as reachability checks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adrago">Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Delete relaxation ignores delete effects. A goal absent at its fixed point is unreachable, but goals that appear may not be jointly achievable. Full BFS retains delete effects and proves unsatisfiability only by exhausting the state space; exhausting the budget means unknown. Relaxation is cheaper but one-sided, while BFS is stricter and limited by search size.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Taking a key may remove a different condition. Two goals can each appear reachable under relaxation even if they cannot hold simultaneously. Full-state search exposes that conflict.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22568">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22568-drago/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-43baaeea36e72a90">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:drago" data-paper-title="Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dd525846f866a39f">Is it enough for a repair to leave the total blocker weight unchanged or lower?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adrago">Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Blocker weight must strictly fall, no blocker dimension may be added, and the goal count must not decrease. Object counts may move only toward the public specification, and a previously solvable specification must not become unsatisfiable or unknown. On rejection the old object is kept and the loop stops. A non-increase rule can accept pointless rewrites, while goal deletion games the diagnostic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Reject a rewrite that merely rewords a specification while leaving both blockers. Also reject a rewrite that reduces blockers by dropping a goal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22568">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.22568-drago/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dd525846f866a39f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:janus" data-paper-title="Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-janus-c8240d07" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-be862a584cf61633">Why does Janus put unexecuted proposals in the research graph?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajanus">Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unexecuted proposals are research directions that can compete for budget. The system estimates value, information gain, and exploration benefit before choosing what to run. The graph also stores actual experimental feedback and abstract skills so later proposals use prior evidence. Predictions guide selection; they do not count as completed experiments or observed scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A model change and a diagnosis of a prior failure can both enter as candidates. Remaining budget determines which one gets compute first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13194-janus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be862a584cf61633">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:janus" data-paper-title="Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d051e2e09bf28dfd">Why compare experimental proposals in pairs and then fit value scores rather than choosing the most compelling description?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajanus">Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pairwise comparisons establish a calibratable ordering for expected value, information gain, and exploration benefit. A sparse tournament fits Bradley–Terry scores to connect local judgments. Predictions allocate the experiment budget; executed successes and failures update the model and skills. A high predicted score is neither a completed experiment nor a substitute for execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Proposal A promises a larger metric gain, while B better rules out a key hypothesis. Adjust exploration weight to the remaining budget rather than treating polished promises as results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13194-janus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d051e2e09bf28dfd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:janus" data-paper-title="Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9e6ceb7d58c0979f">How does selection by predicted gain alone differ from including information gain and exploration benefit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajanus">Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Predicted gain alone favors currently promising regions and may overexploit them. Information gain values ruling out uncertain hypotheses, while exploration benefit gives unknown regions a chance. Janus adjusts weights with progress and remaining budget, but only actual execution can correct prediction errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A promises a small but well-understood gain. B may not improve the metric but can distinguish two mechanisms. Early in the budget, B may be worth testing first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13194-janus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9e6ceb7d58c0979f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:janus" data-paper-title="Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aca159e2d90903f9">How do soft comparisons in a sparse tournament become proposal value scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajanus">Janus: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fit the soft preferences on comparison edges by BCE on sigmoid(g_m-g_n), yielding relative Bradley–Terry scores, then weight the three benefits. This links local preferences without providing absolute success probabilities. The graph and skills update after execution; predictions cannot replace sandbox results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If A slightly beats B and B beats C, fit their relative order. A&#x27;s higher value does not mean its experiment has beaten the best current model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 结果、验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13194-janus/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aca159e2d90903f9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-lookahead" data-paper-title="Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-jev-lookahead-d66c9de4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8e02b08a2591a3de">What do code simulation and model evaluation each do in lookahead?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-lookahead">Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Code executes legal actions on independent copies of the current state and produces actual successor observations. The model compares public consequences and selects an action. This avoids relying solely on textual guesses about transitions, but requires faithful isolation and simulation. Selection itself must not mutate the live environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Open a drawer on a copy to see its contents before deciding whether to open the real one. The scorer need not invent what is inside.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01834-jev-lookahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8e02b08a2591a3de">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-lookahead" data-paper-title="Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bb996b26be801ddf">What does giving newly available successor-state actions add beyond the next observation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-lookahead">Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The next observation describes the immediate change. Newly available actions show which future paths the step unlocks, exposing long-term value in actions without immediate payoff. Code simulates the transition on a cloned state, and the decision model evaluates public consequences only. Simulator reward or the reference plan must not leak into the scorer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Picking up a key does not finish the task, but it enables opening a side door. Seeing that action reveals why the key can matter later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01834-jev-lookahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bb996b26be801ddf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-lookahead" data-paper-title="Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0bcf1b77a4cca239">What does one-step simulation add over semantic action scoring, and why doesn&#x27;t it guarantee optimality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-lookahead">Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Semantic scoring mainly uses action names and the task description. One-step simulation also gives the next observation and newly available actions, revealing unlocked opportunities. It still looks only one step ahead and the scorer may misjudge, so the new action list is not a long-horizon planning oracle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Picking up a key may not seem close to the goal until simulation reveals the open-door action. Unknown obstacles behind the door can still prevent success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01834-jev-lookahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0bcf1b77a4cca239">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-lookahead" data-paper-title="Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3aefdd9ad5723f6">Does returning a different object from fork guarantee branch isolation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-lookahead">Code Owns the Simulation, Jev Owns the Evaluation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The Chinese University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Nested mutable state, random generators, and external resources must also be isolated. Distinct object identities do not justify sharing live files or simulator state. The step exposes only observable text, with no reward, gold plan, or success label. The selected action must be legal and is executed by the caller.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two shallow copies share a backpack list, so picking up a key in the clone mutates the real backpack. Different objects did not isolate lookahead.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.01834-jev-lookahead/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f3aefdd9ad5723f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-spawn" data-paper-title="JevSpawn: Adaptive Agentic Inference through Compositional Action Spaces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-jev-spawn-dc827975" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5a841ad22d666429">What options does JevSpawn preserve when one agent execution path fails?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-spawn">JevSpawn: Adaptive Agentic Inference through Compositional Action Spaces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early judgments in long tasks can be wrong. Spending the entire budget on one action makes contradictory evidence costly. JevSpawn allocates reasoning adaptively by organizing optional actions into retainable composite branches and shifting effort after execution feedback. This preserves alternatives without promising exhaustive search.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Inspecting local data and searching online can both be reasonable. If the first path is blocked, continue the other prepared path rather than starting from a blank plan.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00437">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00437-jev-spawn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5a841ad22d666429">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-spawn" data-paper-title="JevSpawn: Adaptive Agentic Inference through Compositional Action Spaces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-03aec54a5d1918af">Why keep several action branches rather than immediately selecting the highest score from the first distribution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-spawn">JevSpawn: Adaptive Agentic Inference through Compositional Action Spaces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early probabilities can be wrong. Keeping multiple composite branches leaves room to recover after contradictory evidence. New feedback reweights priors and guides future exploration; it does not rewrite past success labels. Branches consume budget, so parallel retention trades compute for lower decision risk rather than searching all possibilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Keep both searching and inspecting local files. If search fails, switch to the retained inspection branch without rebuilding the plan from scratch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00437">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00437-jev-spawn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-03aec54a5d1918af">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-spawn" data-paper-title="JevSpawn: Adaptive Agentic Inference through Compositional Action Spaces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-089d2009fb0016d1">How does branch retention differ from independently resampling plans every round?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-spawn">JevSpawn: Adaptive Agentic Inference through Compositional Action Spaces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retention preserves the probabilities and states of earlier unchosen options for reuse after feedback. Independent resampling can repeat old errors or lose progress. Retention also consumes compute and memory, so more retained candidates do not prove lower cost; compare at equal budgets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After search fails, switch to the existing file-inspection branch. Resampling may suggest the same failed search again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00437">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00437-jev-spawn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-089d2009fb0016d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:jev-spawn" data-paper-title="JevSpawn: Adaptive Agentic Inference through Compositional Action Spaces" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e7e9f27b9bbfb974">Why do p(a)·exp(feedback) updates still need normalization and a branch budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ajev-spawn">JevSpawn: Adaptive Agentic Inference through Compositional Action Spaces</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiplication yields unnormalized weights. Divide by their total to obtain a distribution, then retain branches within budget. Multiplication cannot recover a branch with zero prior mass, and extreme feedback can cause numerical instability. The local test verifies a finite posterior and top-branch retention without calling a Jev checkpoint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two branches begin at one half with feedback 0 and 1. Their weight ratio becomes 1:e; e/2 is not a valid probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00437">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2610.00437-jev-spawn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e7e9f27b9bbfb974">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-reasoning" data-paper-title="Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-meta-reasoning-f28ad63c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-eae12a50db1347c2">How does an object-level worker differ from a meta-reasoning controller?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-reasoning">Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A worker performs task content such as retrieval, coding, or analysis. The controller assesses progress, proposes continuation or branching, compares expected benefits, and dispatches work. Control consumes model-call budget and must count in equal-budget comparisons. Persistent artifacts avoid redoing work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A worker writes a test file. The controller decides whether to fix failures, try another approach, or stop. The outputs and costs differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.38147-meta-reasoning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eae12a50db1347c2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-reasoning" data-paper-title="Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-df8ee4a8b86d9461">Why does the controller use a compact state while keeping full results in artifact memory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-reasoning">Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Control decisions need progress, candidate actions, and remaining budget. Repeating full material in every prompt raises cost. Persistent artifacts hold reusable evidence for on-demand reference. Assess, Propose, Evaluate, and Dispatch divide responsibility for continuing or branching. Compressing control state must not discard actual work.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Two workers each write an analysis. The controller keeps the conclusions and file references, then opens the original artifact when needed instead of repeating it in every turn.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.38147-meta-reasoning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-df8ee4a8b86d9461">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-reasoning" data-paper-title="Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6ef66348377903db">What are the trade-offs of separate Assess, Propose, Evaluate, and Dispatch steps versus a single direct controller?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-reasoning">Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separation clarifies state summarization, candidate generation, comparison, and execution, and makes budget feasibility independently checkable. Extra control steps cost calls and may not pay off for simple tasks. Direct control is compact but can conflate evaluation with execution. Compare all calls and final outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A one-step calculation may not need four rounds of control. In complex research, assessing whether to branch can avoid expensive duplicated experiments.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.38147-meta-reasoning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6ef66348377903db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:meta-reasoning" data-paper-title="Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c44534433f4a5cec">How does the local selector weigh expected value and call cost, and what remains unverified?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ameta-reasoning">Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It rejects actions that exceed the budget, then selects using expected value and call cost. Full artifacts stay in persistent memory while control state stays compact. Expected values are explicit inputs, not success predictions learned from frontier workers. Three-seed diagnostics verify scheduling and state separation only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: With two calls left, a three-call action is infeasible regardless of expected value. Do not dispatch it and hide the budget overrun later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38147">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.38147-meta-reasoning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c44534433f4a5cec">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sage-planner" data-paper-title="SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sage-planner-6e4e53de" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1a809b5b36798f25">Why check preconditions before executing an action in a symbolic action gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asage-planner">SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Preconditions tell whether the current world permits an action. Checking first blocks known illegal or unsafe actions and gives the planner a typed reason. The gate covers only modeled rules. Passing it does not prove real-world safety when rules or state are incomplete.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Grasping requires an empty hand and reachable object. The gate blocks a grasp with a full hand before execution rather than explaining a collision afterward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34268">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.34268-sage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1a809b5b36798f25">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sage-planner" data-paper-title="SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-30cc5def5f86c48d">Why edit only the affected subgoal suffix after a failure rather than rewriting the entire plan?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asage-planner">SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The completed prefix reflects actual execution. A full rewrite can repeat actions or wrongly assume the environment reset. The symbolic gate first blocks invalid preconditions and provides a typed cause; the planner then repairs the affected future steps. Keeping the prefix preserves consistency with the current world, not blind commitment to the old plan.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A cup has been washed, but the cabinet is locked. Revise how to store it rather than washing it again and assuming the cabinet already opened.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34268">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.34268-sage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-30cc5def5f86c48d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sage-planner" data-paper-title="SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-642090c6a6e8840c">What do typed failure causes add over a free-text message saying an action failed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asage-planner">SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Typed causes distinguish missing resources, unmet preconditions, and affected subgoals, allowing a local editor to revise the relevant suffix. Generic text can cause a full rewrite or repetition of completed actions. Structured feedback still depends on accurate symbolic state and does not replace real environment feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A locked cabinet calls for a key or another location; a missing object calls for renewed perception. Those are different recoveries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34268">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.34268-sage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-642090c6a6e8840c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sage-planner" data-paper-title="SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4cc215ec54fd020d">Does a zero-token gate establish a low-cost reproduction of the entire LLM planner?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asage-planner">SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Only the symbolic gate uses no language-model calls. Plan generation and suffix editing still have their own costs. The local run executes the gate and a reference suffix editor, not AI2-THOR. Three-seed fixture success is neither embodied task success nor end-to-end inference cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A Boolean check can refuse to open a cabinet without producing the new plan. Counting only the check misses recovery&#x27;s model calls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34268">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.34268-sage/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4cc215ec54fd020d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searchatlas" data-paper-title="SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-searchatlas-1aefb816" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-86d14a866c7a95dd">Why are edges in a query–evidence–answer graph more explanatory than a list of pages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearchatlas">SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Edges show what evidence a query found and which constraint or answer span it supports. This traces how information reaches the conclusion. A link list records visits without establishing support. Graph extraction itself can be wrong, so an edge is not definitive proof of a fact.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If all sources discuss price, the graph can show no incoming edge for local availability, which is harder to spot in a list of ten links.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.10901-searchatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-86d14a866c7a95dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searchatlas" data-paper-title="SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f159d742140bf711">Why can an evidential query graph reveal a gap after searching many web pages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearchatlas">SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Page count is not constraint coverage. Directed query–evidence–answer relations must show what supports each condition and whether the conclusion crosses an unverified edge. Graph auditing separates repeated evidence from a genuinely completed reasoning chain. A passing graph interface does not establish reliable evidence collection by the search model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Ten pages give a product&#x27;s price, but none confirms regional availability. A claim that it is sold locally still lacks a support edge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.10901-searchatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f159d742140bf711">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searchatlas" data-paper-title="SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ff16d943d79eb7e9">Why are search diversity and constraint coverage different metrics?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearchatlas">SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Diversity measures differences among queries or sources; coverage measures whether evidence supports the requested conditions. Distinct sites can repeat one fact, and a few strong sources can cover several needs. SearchAtlas audits the support structure rather than treating domain counts as evidence chains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Five sites can repeat the same product specifications without covering returns. One official policy page can fill that gap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.10901-searchatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ff16d943d79eb7e9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:searchatlas" data-paper-title="SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2deaaf979c81c85e">Does local validation of evidence-propagation edges include the paper&#x27;s search agents and automatic parser?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asearchatlas">SearchAtlas: Analyzing Agentic Search Strategies via Evidential Query Graphs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Duke University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The local run builds and checks edges on public fixtures and does not run the paper&#x27;s five search agents. The paper&#x27;s edge F1 measures agreement between automatic graph parsing and human annotations, not local QA accuracy. Executing the interface does not establish evidence extraction or fact judgment on real pages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Checking connectivity after being given an edge from Evidence A to Constraint B does not prove the model can extract that relationship from arbitrary web pages.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式或操作, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10901">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2609.10901-searchatlas/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2deaaf979c81c85e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:deeprepro" data-paper-title="DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-deeprepro-1ec5a199" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b5488f16f6f2b49">Why is paper reproduction an evolving software engineering task rather than a translation of formulas?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adeeprepro">DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equations are only part of the specification. Reproduction also involves dependencies, data formats, interfaces, and tests. Each step changes what can follow. DeepRepro studies how to implement and verify within an evolving repository while retaining alignment with the paper, not how to finish by writing one long plan.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The network is implemented, but loading data reveals a new axis-order requirement. The training code must fit that interface rather than blindly following section order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26557">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26557-deeprepro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b5488f16f6f2b49">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:deeprepro" data-paper-title="DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-07944eab0463db0d">Why must a paper-to-code subplan read current repository state rather than following paper order alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adeeprepro">DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Interfaces, dependencies, and files change during implementation. Prior assumptions can expire. Fine-grained subplans use current repository state and execution feedback to decide what to do next. The paper defines the goal; repository state defines what can run. Neither is replaced by one initial checklist.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The next paper step is evaluator integration, but the data interface has changed. Adapt to the new contract instead of generating scripts that no longer connect.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26557">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26557-deeprepro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-07944eab0463db0d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:deeprepro" data-paper-title="DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2b3ad56805903811">What can inspecting artifacts tell you, and what requires rerunning the reproduction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adeeprepro">DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Artifact inspection checks that code, logs, and tests correspond to the named paper and revision, auditing an existing execution. A rerun must actually install dependencies, call models, and run tests to see whether results reproduce now. The evidence scopes differ; a consistent local DeepRepro replay does not replace a full Code-Dev run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A log shows that tests passed on one commit. Repeating the pass in a clean environment still requires installation and execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26557">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26557-deeprepro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2b3ad56805903811">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:deeprepro" data-paper-title="DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8ddcad1b744e2a8">Does artifact replay count as rerunning official PaperBench Code-Dev?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Adeeprepro">DeepRepro: State-Aware Subplanning for Paper-to-Code Reproduction in Evolving Repositories</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Replay reads real exports from a pinned revision and checks plans, execution steps, and test coverage in paper and state order. It does not pay again for model API calls or the full implementation experiment. A perfect deterministic mini-suite verifies the state-driven path only, not official reproduction capability or cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Replaying an old test record shows whether a plan revision covered the failure; it does not regenerate code and run all tests in the current environment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26557">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.26557-deeprepro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8ddcad1b744e2a8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:loongreflect" data-paper-title="LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-loongreflect-7debd709" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-29d2ec8bb15b0afd">Why does a long-horizon search agent need reflection that recovers its route, not just an explanation at the end?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aloongreflect">LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multi-hop evidence gathering includes failed attempts. An early wrong turn can make later steps depend on bad evidence. LoongReflect changes current information and the continuation path so the agent can recover before the task ends. An accurate retrospective cannot improve the evidence gathering of an already completed run.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If search keeps finding reprints of the same article, return to the earlier branch and change sources before submitting, not after admitting the evidence is narrow.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11967">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.11967-loongreflect/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-29d2ec8bb15b0afd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:loongreflect" data-paper-title="LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-47d09fe862087bb4">Why model reflection and backtracking as reversible memory-control actions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aloongreflect">LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long searches must choose external actions, which traces to retain, and which fork to return to. Making reflection and backtracking policy actions lets the agent learn when to change memory. A privileged teacher supplies training signals and outcome reward covers long-run success, but evaluation must not give the student the teacher&#x27;s global view or future answers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After a dead end, return to the previous branch and keep the reason for failure. Appending reflection text without changing trace state is not real backtracking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11967">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.11967-loongreflect/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47d09fe862087bb4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:loongreflect" data-paper-title="LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b29d7bd63cdc6137">How do the fast privileged-teacher channel and slow outcome-GRPO channel supervise different signals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aloongreflect">LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The fast channel distills fine-grained reflection decisions from the teacher&#x27;s view. The slow channel optimizes long-horizon policy using final trajectory outcomes. One provides local guidance, the other tests overall effectiveness. Privileged information belongs only with the training teacher or evaluator; the deployed student cannot read gold outcomes to choose backtracking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A teacher can identify missing evidence at one search step. Final reward checks whether the complete answer succeeds. Online, the student sees only current observations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11967">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.11967-loongreflect/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b29d7bd63cdc6137">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:loongreflect" data-paper-title="LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d989382ef608ad22">Does a low mini-suite average cost establish savings for a real long-context model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aloongreflect">LoongReflect: Boosting Long-Horizon Reflection in Search Agents via Global Perspective Distillation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The deterministic suite verifies reflection, backtracking, and state transitions without a real browser, external tools, or the paper&#x27;s large model. Cost follows the diagnostic definition. When accuracy is saturated, inspect branches and traces; proxy counts do not translate directly into real tokens or API fees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A rule branch billed a fraction of a cost unit does not mean real model reflection uses the same fraction of tokens or time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11967">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.11967-loongreflect/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d989382ef608ad22">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toollift" data-paper-title="ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-toollift-dbb897af" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-aa0bc3a2fde6af6b">What experience does ToolLIFT transfer when tool sets change frequently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoollift">ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>API names, arguments, and response formats change across services, but functional steps can stay stable, such as checking identity before reading records. ToolLIFT retains that procedural structure and resolves it against the current tool catalog rather than discarding old traces. Concrete interfaces must still be checked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A migration still requires finding a customer before retrieving orders, but the old function names and fields cannot be copied into the new service.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03468">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.03468-toollift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aa0bc3a2fde6af6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toollift" data-paper-title="ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-830b9099c62167a8">Why does lifting a trajectory into a function workflow graph help reuse it with new tools?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoollift">ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The graph preserves required operations and dependencies while deferring concrete tools and interfaces until execution. A new tool set can implement the same functional plan using its current schemas. Parameter contracts still matter; each node needs a real tool with the required input/output behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Old search_web and new lookup can implement evidence retrieval, so the workflow can be reused, but arguments and response formats must be matched again.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03468">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.03468-toollift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-830b9099c62167a8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toollift" data-paper-title="ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9cee31815ddb00c9">What information does a function workflow graph need versus an executable tool plan?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoollift">ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The function graph describes desired operations and state dependencies, preserving procedure across catalogs. An executable plan must also bind each node to a current API, parameters, and actual objects. The first gives transferable abstraction and the second grounds it. A sensible graph does not guarantee valid arguments, and legal calls need not cover the whole task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The graph says find customer then find orders. Execution must confirm whether the new service returns customer_id or account_id and which field the order API accepts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03468">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.03468-toollift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9cee31815ddb00c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:toollift" data-paper-title="ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8419e689fae8c59">Why preserve state dependencies in Lift and Select rather than saving only a list of functions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atoollift">ToolLIFT: Lifting Tool-Specific Trajectories into Function-Level Graphs for Generalizable Tool Planning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Authors did not disclose affiliation</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Edges show what evidence or object each later step needs, and Select chooses tools based on current state. An unordered list loses variable provenance and preconditions. The mini-suite verifies lifting and selection control flow without real tools; perfect fixture scores do not establish transfer to unseen services.</p>
