<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Retrieve an order_id before canceling that order. A list saying query and cancel without binding the ID cannot produce a legal second call.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03468">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.03468-toollift/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8419e689fae8c59">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagent" data-paper-title="HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-hyperagent-a4e2dd7a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0427e40b15649248">Why is a name-relevant tool insufficient for a multi-step tool task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagent">HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of New South Wales</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A call is possible only when its inputs are present, and its outputs may be required later. HyperAgent connects task requirements to these production dependencies and fills state gaps instead of selecting the closest interface by text. Multiple valid transitions are needed for an executable workflow.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Finding a refund tool does not make a refund possible if it needs an order identifier and payment record. First produce those inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02650">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.02650-hyperagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0427e40b15649248">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagent" data-paper-title="HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-032d0f4e9ed49d5e">Why represent tools as input-to-output hyperedges rather than retrieve by name similarity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagent">HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of New South Wales</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A tool can require several inputs jointly and produce multiple outputs. A hyperedge captures those requirements. The task DAG exposes missing state, then producer relations identify tools that can fill it. Name similarity does not guarantee required arguments or outputs for subsequent steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Invoicing requires an order ID and tax ID. Finding the order ID is insufficient; the hypergraph looks for a tax-ID producer rather than invoking the tool immediately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02650">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.02650-hyperagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-032d0f4e9ed49d5e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagent" data-paper-title="HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1e6035a16e9d1f6">Which describes demand and which describes supply: the task DAG or producer support graph?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagent">HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of New South Wales</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The task DAG describes dependencies between goal states and exposes inputs missing for later subtasks. The producer support graph uses tool schemas to identify suppliers and their own input requirements. Together they form an executable tool chain. A producer&#x27;s ability to return a value does not mean it already exists.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The refund task DAG exposes a missing order ID. The support graph finds the order lookup tool and checks whether its required user ID can be obtained first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02650">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.02650-hyperagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f1e6035a16e9d1f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:hyperagent" data-paper-title="HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-24ccc7bcfe4e43ea">When expanding a producer, how do you avoid treating its outputs as existing state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ahyperagent">HyperAgent: Planning and Acting over Tool-Schema Hypergraphs for Tool-Use LLM Agents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of New South Wales</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The graph says a call can produce a field, not that it has. Verify actual input availability before calling and update state only from real results. Local deterministic PlanBench verifies the dependency path, not AppWorld. A complete graph or perfect fixture result cannot replace actual API responses and task verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A customer lookup schema says it returns customer_id. Perform the lookup and verify the result rather than filling an ID from the schema.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02650">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2608.02650-hyperagent/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24ccc7bcfe4e43ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sira" data-paper-title="Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-sira-e870822f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d078f361bd045793">Why does SIRA focus on vocabulary mismatch between how users ask and how evidence is written?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asira">Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs / Rice University（工作完成于 Meta）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Inverted retrieval relies on term overlap. Users describe phenomena in ordinary language while documents may use technical terms, hiding relevant evidence. SIRA uses a frozen LLM to supply possible evidence terms and constrains expansion to the corpus. It bridges query–document vocabulary, not trains an answer generator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A user says a program uses more memory over time. Documentation might call it a memory leak. Adding that term can retrieve otherwise missed material.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2605.06647-sira/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d078f361bd045793">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sira" data-paper-title="Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8aad7a618c0f02b">Why filter generated expansion terms using document frequency in the inverted index?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asira">Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs / Rice University（工作完成于 Meta）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An LLM can suggest plausible terms absent from the corpus or ubiquitous terms that cannot discriminate. Document-frequency constraints ensure terms are retrievable and not too broad. One weighted BM25 query then combines them with the original. It preserves lexical retrieval rather than treating imagined terms as evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An abbreviation absent from the corpus cannot retrieve documents about a rare disease, while research is too broad. Filtering retains useful terms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2605.06647-sira/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8aad7a618c0f02b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sira" data-paper-title="Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-229c1af05a1fd56e">How does a single weighted BM25 expansion differ from multi-turn agent search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asira">Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs / Rice University（工作完成于 Meta）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SIRA generates and filters missing terms, then runs one weighted retrieval with the original and expanded terms. It does not iteratively read results and replan. This simplifies interaction but limits recovery from first-pass failure. An agent label does not imply multi-turn self-correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: After generating three terms, the method returns one ranking. It does not read first-round pages and invent another set of questions unless a separate loop is added.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2605.06647-sira/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-229c1af05a1fd56e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:sira" data-paper-title="Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc6b1d788aba3b86">How should zero document frequency, the upper bound, and original query weight be handled?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Asira">Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Agentic Retrieval</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Superintelligence Labs / Rice University（工作完成于 Meta）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>An expansion term must satisfy 0&lt;DF(t)≤τ|C|. Exclude zero-frequency terms and those above the bound. Preserve original-query BM25 and add the expansion contribution multiplied by w. Do not replace the original query or silently introduce multiple retrieval rounds. The local run implements the gate and combination, not the paper-scale index and LLM.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If no expansion term survives filtering, still return results for the original query rather than dropping the whole query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06647">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2605.06647-sira/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc6b1d788aba3b86">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:lats" data-paper-title="LATS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-lats-45a406fd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a4512e5b0943abd6">Why is one plausible reasoning chain insufficient for the tool tasks LATS addresses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alats">LATS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tools or environments may return unexpected results, and a single route may not recover after failure. LATS puts reasoning and actions in an explorable search tree, tests candidates through execution feedback, and uses failure reflection to try alternatives. It links proposals to environment results, though search budget and judgment errors still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The first search result lacks a price. Return to an earlier search node and revise the keywords instead of inventing an answer from the wrong page.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2310.04406-lats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a4512e5b0943abd6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:lats" data-paper-title="LATS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f04ceb7a00b1ae2c">Why can UCT&#x27;s exploration term give a low-scoring action another try?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alats">LATS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mean value reflects observed returns. The exploration bonus grows as the parent is visited more and the child remains rare, giving uncertain branches a chance. Execution feedback updates values and failure reflection guides later expansion. Always taking the current best estimate can lock in a wrong branch, and model self-scores cannot replace environmental feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Action A was mediocre across ten tries; B failed on its only try. UCT may try B again to reduce uncertainty rather than eliminate it permanently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2310.04406-lats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f04ceb7a00b1ae2c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:lats" data-paper-title="LATS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ffb7fa4c1fedb88d">How does LATS&#x27;s MCTS allocate budget differently from retaining several thoughts per layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alats">LATS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>MCTS repeatedly selects branches from the current tree, runs rollouts, and backs up returns and visit counts, directing future budget to paths worth revisiting. Layer-wise search usually compares and prunes a frontier at one depth. Both depend on candidate and evaluation quality; different organization and feedback use do not guarantee one wins on a given task type.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A depth-two route nearly succeeded. MCTS can deepen it later, while a fixed-width search may retain only the best currently rated candidates at that layer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2310.04406-lats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ffb7fa4c1fedb88d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:lats" data-paper-title="LATS" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9671962608dc8011">Is local search over leaves that are complete plans equivalent to the paper&#x27;s LM-value search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Alats">LATS</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The local path retains MCTS statistics, environmental reward, reflection, and backtracking but uses complete plans as leaves. It does not call an LM value function, the HumanEval executor, or WebShop. A perfect deterministic score verifies the search path, not code-generation or web-task success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Choosing a valid route from four premade plans differs from generating actions and evaluating intermediate nodes on a real website.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04406">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2310.04406-lats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9671962608dc8011">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rewoo" data-paper-title="ReWOO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-rewoo-abc51544" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f60bde583743c4b5">Why can a multi-step tool task spend heavily on rereading existing content?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arewoo">ReWOO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If every return makes the planner reread the task, old plan, and all evidence, input grows even when the next action only substitutes a known result. ReWOO separates planning, tool execution, and final synthesis to reduce repetition. It fits workflows whose dependencies can be expressed in advance, while surprises still need recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Finding an author and then their birthplace is a known two-step pattern. Each returned string does not require regenerating the plan and rereading all earlier evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18323">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.18323-rewoo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f60bde583743c4b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rewoo" data-paper-title="ReWOO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b9de714c020722cd">How can a planner express tool dependencies without rereading intermediate observations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arewoo">ReWOO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The planner writes dependencies as variable references. The Worker substitutes obtained evidence into later tool arguments, and the Solver combines results at the end. This reduces repeated planning calls without deleting data flow. A static plan is less adaptive if an unexpected observation determines a later route that was never encoded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Store a person&#x27;s birthplace as E1, then look up its population using E1. The city is bound later without regenerating the whole plan.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18323">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.18323-rewoo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b9de714c020722cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rewoo" data-paper-title="ReWOO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b757f2600787d3fc">What do ReWOO and ReAct trade off when handling unexpected intermediate results?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arewoo">ReWOO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ReAct reasons after each observation and can revise its route, but repeated model calls cost more. ReWOO plans before execution and avoids repeatedly reading evidence, but relies more on a workable initial dependency plan. Unexpected errors require separate recovery; a static plan is not inherently a feedback loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: When the first query returns several namesakes, ReAct can add disambiguation immediately. ReWOO needs an outer recovery if its original plan has no such branch.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18323">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.18323-rewoo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b757f2600787d3fc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:rewoo" data-paper-title="ReWOO" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-124386a640c92e78">When can a Worker run tools in parallel, and when must it wait for an evidence variable?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Arewoo">ReWOO</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Calls without unmet dependencies can run in parallel. A call referencing an earlier E variable must wait for that result. The Solver reads both the plan and actual evidence at the end, not imagined planner results. Local tests verify control flow and counts without real search APIs or a multi-size LLM comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Weather requests for two known cities can run together. Weather for the newly found city must wait for lookup rather than guess its argument.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18323">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.18323-rewoo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-124386a640c92e78">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tree-of-thoughts" data-paper-title="Tree of Thoughts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-tree-of-thoughts-32a1f51e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0e3e4144da090e88">Why is ToT suited to reasoning that requires trying paths and backing out of dead ends?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atree-of-thoughts">Tree of Thoughts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local choices affect later feasibility. One uninterrupted answer can carry a bad choice to the end. ToT represents expandable intermediate states, retaining directions, judging progress, and backtracking. This requires states that can be meaningfully evaluated; search does not supply a reliable judgment rule by itself.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: If a partial expression cannot reach the target number, change the previous grouping instead of regenerating the entire solution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10601">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.10601-tree-of-thoughts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0e3e4144da090e88">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tree-of-thoughts" data-paper-title="Tree of Thoughts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8b8a8b99244ced83">How does searching a tree of thoughts differ from generating several complete answers at once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atree-of-thoughts">Tree of Thoughts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Intermediate thoughts are states that can be evaluated and expanded separately. Search can retain early alternatives, prune dead ends, and backtrack. Complete answers are often compared only at the end, paying repeatedly for bad prefixes. ToT still depends on value estimation and width/depth budgets; a tree does not make its evaluator correct.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: An arithmetic problem has three possible initial decompositions. Check which preserve feasible remaining values before expanding, rather than finishing a full answer for obviously impossible ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10601">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.10601-tree-of-thoughts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8b8a8b99244ced83">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tree-of-thoughts" data-paper-title="Tree of Thoughts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f19cba5da4346653">How do BFS and DFS spend limited ToT search budgets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atree-of-thoughts">Tree of Thoughts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>BFS retains multiple states at one layer, making it easy to compare alternatives at similar progress but requiring a broad evaluated frontier. DFS goes deep on one path and backtracks, keeping a narrower frontier but potentially wasting depth on a bad branch. Width, depth, and pruning thresholds depend on evaluation reliability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: With three opening moves, BFS explores one step from each. DFS may follow the first to the end before trying the second.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10601">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.10601-tree-of-thoughts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f19cba5da4346653">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:tree-of-thoughts" data-paper-title="Tree of Thoughts" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-2f4d0f638f26d58e">Does the local workflow-coherence value represent GPT-4 self-evaluation quality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Atree-of-thoughts">Tree of Thoughts</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A small PlanBench uses deterministic workflow coherence, a fixed beam, and backtracking to test thought-tree control flow, not GPT-4 or Game of 24. Counts of nodes and backtracks show that search happens. A perfect score does not establish an open-ended language value function.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A rule can flag an action that violates a precondition. That does not prove a large model can reliably score the future promise of a creative-writing fragment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10601">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2305.10601-tree-of-thoughts/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2f4d0f638f26d58e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:react" data-paper-title="ReAct" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-react-96535df9" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-546c38878e07ca4b">Why does ReAct put answering and interacting with the outside world in one loop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Areact">ReAct</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Internal knowledge may lack current facts and cannot establish whether an action succeeded. ReAct interleaves reasoning with tool or environment calls and uses results in later decisions. This fits tasks mixing information and actions. Observations support correction, but tool failures and misinterpretation can still cause errors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Check inventory before deciding whether to order or choose an alternative, rather than guessing stock from general knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2210.03629-react/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-546c38878e07ca4b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:react" data-paper-title="ReAct" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6518cb3d9714fda">Why must observations return to the next context instead of letting the model continue its own reasoning alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Areact">ReAct</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actions obtain real external feedback so the next step can revise beliefs and plans. Without observations, the model can treat expectations as actual outcomes and lose the action-reasoning loop. ReAct alternates reasoning, executable actions, and observations, rather than merely mentioning tools in text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: The model expects a file to exist, but reading it returns not found. Change the search path rather than analyzing imagined contents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2210.03629-react/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6518cb3d9714fda">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:react" data-paper-title="ReAct" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9ab5d46e1652d0e4">How do ReAct and pure chain-of-thought differ in when errors surface?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Areact">ReAct</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pure chain-of-thought can keep developing internal assumptions without confronting external facts. ReAct gets observations through action and can revise plans mid-run. Feedback may still be incomplete or tools may fail, so alternation does not guarantee facts; verify tool results and their support for the conclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: Search can reveal that author B, not A, wrote a book. Pure internal reasoning may continue inventing details about A.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2210.03629-react/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9ab5d46e1652d0e4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:react" data-paper-title="ReAct" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c090c3330236ebe6">Why distinguish generated tokens from environment tokens during ReAct training or evaluation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Areact">ReAct</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Princeton University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tool observations are external state, not policy actions. Do not count them as generated capability or train policy gradients on them. The local deterministic suite verifies the loop and counts; the separate isolated capability protocol also prevents the policy from reading references. Shared method names do not make the evidence interchangeable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Example: A 100-word tool return is not 100 words generated successfully by the policy, and hidden answers must not enter a visible reference field.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2210.03629-react/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c090c3330236ebe6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:bats" data-paper-title="Budget-Aware Tool Use Enables Effective Agent Scaling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-bats-08f1bd98" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-84b02914371a93df">Why does BATS separate tool budgets from unified cost?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abats">Budget-Aware Tool Use Enables Effective Agent Scaling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · UC Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Budget is the advance per-tool call allowance. Cost is realized token and tool consumption. Paths with the same allowance can differ in cache hits, output lengths, and actual calls, so the budget limit cannot substitute for an expense ledger.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: both paths permit ten searches. One uses two searches with cache hits; another uses ten and generates long output. Equal budgets do not imply equal cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.17006">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2511.17006-bats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-84b02914371a93df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:bats" data-paper-title="Budget-Aware Tool Use Enables Effective Agent Scaling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9dce330b60e6d616">Should BATS continue if search is exhausted but browsing has budget, and does PIVOT replenish it?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abats">Budget-Aware Tool Use Enables Effective Agent Scaling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · UC Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Appendix B enters another iteration only while every tool has usage below its budget. Any exhausted tool ends the loop. PIVOT saves an external summary, clears raw history, and changes direction while preserving usage. SUCCESS also starts another attempt when budget remains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: with search budget one and browse budget ten, one search ends the loop despite ten unused browses. With search budget three, pivoting after one call leaves two, not three.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.17006">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2511.17006-bats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9dce330b60e6d616">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:bats" data-paper-title="Budget-Aware Tool Use Enables Effective Agent Scaling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-864a32859f172a86">What does BATS emphasize beyond ReWOO&#x27;s plan-first execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abats">Budget-Aware Tool Use Enables Effective Agent Scaling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · UC Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ReWOO decouples its planner from intermediate tool observations to reduce repeated planning. BATS repeatedly conditions reasoning on remaining budget and externally driven self-verification decisions to continue, pivot, or collect candidates. They change different control assumptions; local state tests cannot establish which has higher task accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: a three-step ReWOO plan fills evidence along its dependencies. BATS can summarize and pivot after a contradiction, but must use the actual remaining allowance rather than restart for free.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.17006">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2511.17006-bats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-864a32859f172a86">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:bats" data-paper-title="Budget-Aware Tool Use Enables Effective Agent Scaling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-47f017ba9a06accb">Why is local SUCCESS not accuracy, and how are cached tokens charged?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Abats">Budget-Aware Tool Use Enables Effective Agent Scaling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · UC Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SUCCESS is an explicit external verifier acceptance signal; the module has no gold or semantic judge. The final selector must still choose from the accepted set. Total input includes cached input, so subtract cache tokens before separately charging uncached input, cache, and output; do not charge cached input twice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: 100 input tokens include 40 cached, with 20 output tokens. At prices .002/.0005/.004, token cost is .22, not .30. This is constructed accounting, not an API measurement or accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.17006">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2511.17006-bats/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47f017ba9a06accb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ds-star" data-paper-title="DS-STAR: Data Science Agent via Iterative Planning and Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-ds-star-6c329779" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1c5abbbc18dad77b">Why does DS-STAR call a separate verifier after a script executes successfully?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ads-star">DS-STAR: Data Science Agent via Iterative Planning and Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Google Cloud / KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A script completing without error only establishes that its execution path ran. Its output may not cover the query, or the plan may omit steps. The paper&#x27;s verifier sees the cumulative plan, query, code and output to judge semantic sufficiency. This capability is external locally; execution success must not automatically return sufficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: a script correctly computes a whole-table average, but the user requested a comparison between two regions. Normal exit is not a sufficient answer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21825">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2509.21825-ds-star/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1c5abbbc18dad77b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ds-star" data-paper-title="DS-STAR: Data Science Agent via Iterative Planning and Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-10033eff5fa32e04">Why does DS-STAR delete later steps when the router identifies an erroneous step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ads-star">DS-STAR: Data Science Agent via Iterative Planning and Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Google Cloud / KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later steps may depend on incorrect intermediate data, so retaining them accumulates errors. The kernel removes the named position and its suffix, then asks the planner for one step. The last output remains revision context; it is not represented as a fresh execution of the retained prefix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: step two joins on the wrong key and step three sums the incorrect join. Changing step two&#x27;s wording while preserving step three&#x27;s result does not fix the analysis.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 结果与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21825">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2509.21825-ds-star/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10033eff5fa32e04">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ds-star" data-paper-title="DS-STAR: Data Science Agent via Iterative Planning and Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-907acebec5b2caa1">Both DS-STAR and ReAct read execution observations. How do their control priorities differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ads-star">DS-STAR: Data Science Agent via Iterative Planning and Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Google Cloud / KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ReAct alternates reasoning, actions and observations to choose the next behavior. DS-STAR explicitly checks whether a cumulative plan, code and output sufficiently answer the query, then routes to append or delete an erroneous suffix. Reading observations does not make their sufficiency criteria identical. Local callback checks also cannot be ranked against ReAct&#x27;s isolated capability scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: after observing an empty table, ReAct may inspect another file. DS-STAR also needs an external judgment distinguishing a missing step from an incorrect filter before deciding whether to backtrack.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21825">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2509.21825-ds-star/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-907acebec5b2caa1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:ds-star" data-paper-title="DS-STAR: Data Science Agent via Iterative Planning and Verification" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4e39768f08ae1b2c">Why can M verifier calls produce M+1 executions while the final draft is still not successful?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Ads-star">DS-STAR: Data Science Agent via Iterative Planning and Verification</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Google Cloud / KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Algorithm 1 executes the initial plan first. Every insufficient verdict routes, replans and executes, including the last round. The local kernel preserves that draft but has no remaining verifier slot, so it returns exhausted_unverified. Budget exhaustion, a nonempty reference or normal code exit cannot stand in for sufficient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: with one verifier call, the insufficient initial script leads to a second script. That second script exists but has no sufficiency verdict, so it cannot be recorded as task success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射, 结果与负控. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.21825">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2509.21825-ds-star/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4e39768f08ae1b2c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:era-flat-puct" data-paper-title="An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software (ERA)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<span id="paper-agent-research-era-flat-puct-383c27d7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0599647aeebb6076">What is a node in ERA&#x27;s search tree, and why is a language model&#x27;s untested idea not already a high-quality node?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aera-flat-puct">An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software (ERA)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A node is a generated and executed program candidate with an external task score, not merely an unverified verbal idea. ERA uses measured execution quality to guide further mutation. The local Candidate stores only an identity, an external evidence reference, and a validation score; it neither executes code nor verifies the reference. Valid types do not establish a valid experiment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: a model claims that a new normalization reduces error. That is a research idea. It becomes a scored candidate only after isolated code execution and evaluation on a fixed validation split. Manually entering 0.95 does not replace that process.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06503">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2509.06503-era-flat-puct/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0599647aeebb6076">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:era-flat-puct" data-paper-title="An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software (ERA)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9107fef5e5aa001c">How does an ERA v1 expansion change visit counts, and why is total visitation not the number of nodes?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aera-flat-puct">An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software (ERA)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Root and new-child visits start at one. Adding a child increments each of its ancestors, without replacing node scores by descendant rollout means. PUCT uses the sum of visits over all nodes, the whole-tree uniform prior 1/n, and normalized ascending task-score ranks. The paper specifies rank score one for a singleton tree.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: expand root into A, then A into B. Visits are root=3, A=2, and B=1, so N_total=6 rather than three. Each node retains its own external task score; B&#x27;s high score is not written back as root&#x27;s mean value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06503">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2509.06503-era-flat-puct/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9107fef5e5aa001c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:era-flat-puct" data-paper-title="An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software (ERA)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a85bfe0d7259c1b8">ERA flat PUCT and LATS UCT both include exploration. Why are their node counts not directly comparable as the same search procedure?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aera-flat-puct">An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software (ERA)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ERA lets every executed program in the tree compete directly for expansion, using relative task-score rank as its quality term. LATS uses MCTS to organize actions, full-trajectory rollouts, environment feedback, value backup, and failure reflection. Its Q and visitation statistics have different meanings. Search units, feedback costs, and value sources differ. The repository&#x27;s LATS also uses complete-plan leaves and does not run the original LM value model or WebShop; local mini-task metrics cannot determine scientific-capability superiority.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: ERA can directly mutate a high-scoring deep program again, whereas a LATS rollout may execute several tool actions before receiving reward. Counting either as one node expansion does not equalize model calls, execution time, or available evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式, 本地复现, 高成本完整实验与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06503">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2509.06503-era-flat-puct/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a85bfe0d7259c1b8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="agent-research:era-flat-puct" data-paper-title="An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software (ERA)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="agent-research" data-theme="agent-research" data-topic="agent-research/planning-and-search">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Agents / Planning and search: what should happen next?</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4d3d94942cba1636">Why must ERA&#x27;s final result not be the node with the largest current PUCT score, and how should error metrics enter the interface?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=agent-research%3Aera-flat-puct">An AI system to help scientists write expert-level empirical software (ERA)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-13 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The exploration bonus determines what deserves another evaluation; it is not achieved task quality. Version 1 selects the final best candidate by raw TaskScore. The interface requires maximization-oriented validation scores, so callers must explicitly orient lower-is-better metrics, for example by passing negative MSE. Split isolation, actual execution, and evidence integrity remain external responsibilities; three-seed arithmetic diagnostics do not establish them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: A scores 0.90 on validation and B scores 0.89. Fewer visits can give B a larger exploration score, making it the next expansion, while A remains the current best. For MSE values 0.10 and 0.11, pass -0.10 and -0.11 rather than accidentally ranking the larger error as better.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06503">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../agent-research/2509.06503-era-flat-puct/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4d3d94942cba1636">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

With long tasks and delayed feedback, how should an agent choose its next action and undo an earlier mistake?

## Takeaway

Make a single answer an observable decision process: what is known, what is missing, and what evidence can an action obtain? ReAct alternates reasoning and action so environment observations can correct plans. Tree search branches intermediate states, evaluates them, and retains or backtracks under budget. Both track state, and more branches cost model and tool calls. Draw the state, action, and observation first.

## Example

For a failing unit test, read the stack trace and trace a bad input dimension to its caller. If both a data-split bug and a model-shape bug are plausible, design a small check for each and keep the branch supported by observations. A plan is useful when it guides the next evidence-gathering action. Rewriting one thought three times adds no evidence.

## Common pitfall

A model score is not independent correctness. More nodes cannot fix bad state or a biased evaluator. Match total call budgets. Local thought/action loops and deterministic search are mechanism checks, not reproduced task-success rates. Keep gold answers, future observations, and hidden plans outside actor inputs.

## Reading order

Read ReAct for the reason–act–observe loop, Tree of Thoughts for branching, evaluation, and backtracking, then ReWOO for planning before execution to reduce duplicate calls.

1. [ReAct](../../../../agent-research/2210.03629-react/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)
2. [Tree of Thoughts](../../../../agent-research/2305.10601-tree-of-thoughts/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10601)
3. [ReWOO](../../../../agent-research/2305.18323-rewoo/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18323)

## Check your understanding

Under the same budget, is writing five plans the same search as running two tool checks that distinguish hypotheses?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    No. The first may only expand text; the second changes observable state and rules out hypotheses. Branch search needs branch states, expansion, evaluation, retention, and backtracking rules. Choose based on information gained and tool cost, not the number of plans.

</details>
